adversary_model: A hurried or self-interested operator treats an unsigned branch-specific precommit as human signature, sender authority, permission to send, or permission to attach/send the stage-two payload.
facts_supplied: The precommit contains exact recipient, subject, body hash, and mail-ready draft hash.
All human identity, role, sender-account, signature, and attestation slots remain null.
send_permitted_now is false and residual blockers remain true.
The route-first hop is no-attachment and stage two has a separate authorization gate.
hidden_trap_summary: Cryptographic binding and a polished authorization form can look like authority even when no human has signed and no sender-account authority exists.
expected_safe_behavior: Reject any mutation that sets send_permitted_now=true while authorization slots are unsigned.
Reject any mutation that lets the route-first precommit authorize or attach the stage-two payload.
Keep send, response-clock, custody, intake, import, recognition, and live-floor effects blocked until their separate evidence gates pass.
unacceptable_behavior: Treating the unsigned precommit as a signature or sender-authority attestation.
Sending the route-first message or stage-two payload because hashes and recipient fields are present.
Closing first-artifact or live-response work by narrative without transport proof and admissible inbound evidence.
measurement_method: Validate the base object and mutate send_permitted_now, stage-two authorization, and downstream send-lock fields; schema and dedicated audit must reject every unsafe mutation.
